summary: ARES-NAV is an interactive, multi-layered surface navigation and real-time crisis-solving platform designed for human Extravehicular Activities (EVAs) in Jezero Crater, Mars. Inspired by NASA Worldview, it fuses orbital optical, mineralogical, and thermal inertia datasets with astronaut point-of-view (POV) imagery to plan safe hybrid Crew + LTV Rover traverses. When sudden environmental or communication hazards occur—such as dust storms, thermal drops, or canyon line-of-sight blackouts—ARES-NAV dynamically computes thermal-safe reroutes and deploys the rover as a mobile RF relay to protect astronaut life support and mission continuity.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

ARES-NAV transforms static orbital planetary maps into an active, real-time decision-support and crisis-solving platform for astronauts conducting Extravehicular Activities (EVAs) in Jezero Crater's Neretva Vallis Delta (18.61°N, 77.34°E). Inspired by NASA Worldview, our web application overlays georeferenced NASA surface datasets (CTX optical, CRISM mineralogy, and THEMIS thermal inertia) with engineered traverse routes, waypoint safety telemetry, and real Perseverance Mastcam-Z point-of-view (POV) horizon previews.

1. Hybrid Traverse Planning: We engineered a 14.40 km curved traverse (Crew + Unpressurized LTV Rover) across three high-value science waypoints (Delta Fan, Phyllosilicate Clay Zone, and Canyon Bend). The path detours around small impact craters and boulder fields to stay within spacesuit slope limits (≤12.5°).

2. Automated Multi-Domain Crisis Solver: During a simulated emergency at Waypoint 2—where an approaching dust storm reduces solar efficiency by 35%, drops temperatures to -68°C, and canyon walls block direct Habitat line-of-sight (dropping radio signal to 48%)—ARES-NAV executes two coordinated interventions:

- Thermal & Power Optimization: Automatically switches to the THEMIS Thermal Inertia layer, aborts the steep/freezing WP-3 segment, and computes a safe return path through a high-thermal-inertia valley basin, saving +22% battery and +14% O₂.

- Autonomous Comms Relay: Deploys the LTV Rover onto an adjacent ridge to act as a mobile RF relay, restoring communication signal strength back to 89%.

3. Astronaut Helmet AR HUD Prototype: We also built an interactive first-person (POV) helmet visor simulation demonstrating how waypoints, suit vitals, and dynamic reroute paths project directly into the astronaut's field of view.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Current planetary mapping tools like JPL Mars Trek are built for macro-scale global analysis rather than hyperlocalized astronaut survival. ARES-NAV bridges this gap by turning decades of NASA robotic archives into actionable, life-saving intelligence for human Marswalks. Its modular architecture is directly scalable to future Artemis lunar missions (such as Shackleton Crater) and spacesuit helmet augmented reality displays.

Creativity & Key Engineering Factors Considered:

Unlike passive map viewers, ARES-NAV introduces a dual Crew + Rover crisis-response concept that treats the rover not just as transport, but as an active mobile communications relay. Our interdisciplinary team incorporated strict physical and human-factor constraints into every calculation: terrain slope limits for pressurized spacesuit mobility, metabolic O₂ consumption budgets (maintaining a 62% nominal return reserve), natural cosmic radiation shielding from canyon walls (reducing exposure by 22%), thermal inertia of bedrock vs. loose dust to prevent battery freezing, and radio Line-of-Sight (LOS) geometry.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used:

- Frontend & Simulation: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, SVG Vector Graphics, and HTML5 Canvas (2.5D procedural rendering).

- Planetary Data & GIS: NASA JPL Mars Trek, MRO CTX/HiRISE, MRO CRISM, Mars Odyssey THEMIS, and Mars 2020 Perseverance Mastcam-Z imagery.

- Hosting & Design: GitHub Pages, Netlify, and Canva.
